UnitStatement: CONTRACT is the authoritative catalog of binding invariants for the Chirality project execution system.
Binding invariants are enforceable constraints for agents and tooling and human processes.
Each binding invariant includes an enforcement point describing where and how compliance is checked.
Invariant IDs using the K-* form are stable and never reused.
Retired invariants are moved to section 3 with retirement rationale.
Section 1 lists all K-* identifiers defined in the invariant catalog with their definition locations.
The invariant catalog defines 21 stable invariants across 10 subsections.
Projects are decomposed as flat packages containing deliverables with no nesting and no phases layer.
K-HIER-1 is enforced through PROJECT_DECOMP gates and PREPARATION folder creation and human review.
Deliverable IDs are stable and persist across path changes.
A deliverable path is a physical projection of decomposition and is not identity.
K-ID-1 is enforced by PROJECT_DECOMP ID assignment and by all agents when referencing IDs.
Only humans author binding approval records.
Agents may not claim to certify or approve or sign or seal or issue work for reliance.
K-AUTH-1 is enforced by agent instruction constraints and human review.
Approvals bind to a specific git SHA.
A content change after approval voids the approval.
K-AUTH-2 is enforced by human review and future SHA comparison tooling.
Approvals are always binding and only binding.
Non-binding guidance is allowed outside approval records.
K-BIND-1 is enforced by human process discipline.
Type 2 agent execution is forbidden before context is sealed and gate-approved by a human.
K-SEAL-1 is enforced by ORCHESTRATOR seal checks and human gate approval.
Type 2 agent context is limited to folder contents and declared references.
Ghost inputs are forbidden for Type 2 agent context.
K-GHOST-1 is enforced by agent instruction constraints for WRITE_SCOPE and _REFERENCES.md and by human review of diffs.
Deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv are authoritative for dependencies.
There is no central dependency graph.
Dependency aggregation occurs on demand via _Reconciliation/.
K-DEP-1 is enforced by TASK+dependency-extract local writes and read-only RECONCILIATION aggregation.
Dependency references to deliverables must resolve to existing deliverable IDs.
Unresolvable dependency targets use TargetType=UNKNOWN.
K-DEP-2 is enforced by TASK+dependency-extract Function 2 and validation checks.
_STATUS.md is the canonical human-readable lifecycle state file for each deliverable.
No file other than _STATUS.md determines deliverable state.
K-STATUS-1 is enforced by all agents reading _STATUS.md and transition rules in SPEC.md Section 3.3.
Upstream changes propagate staleness to all transitive dependent deliverables.
K-STALE-1 is enforced by future staleness calculation tooling and human triage.
Stale items must be triaged by a human before being considered current.
Stale item resolution modes are no impact clear flag and needs rework and needs review.
K-STALE-2 is enforced by the human triage queue.
A deliverable is dirty if any governed input has changed since its last approved SHA.
K-VAL-1 is enforced by future SHA comparison tooling and human review.
Gates are dynamic per project instance.
Minimum required gates are seal transition and pipeline run approval.
Additional gates are project-configurable.
K-GATE-1 is enforced by the ORCHESTRATOR gate map and human configuration.
Merge to main is allowed only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA for the relevant run.
K-MERGE-1 is enforced by human review and a future CI check.
Every non-trivial governed claim must cite evidence with a source path and best-effort section reference or carry explicit location TBD.
Dependency rows are a schema-specific instance of the provenance rule.
Dependency rows use EvidenceFile and SourceRef under SPEC.md Section 6.5.
K-PROV-1 is enforced by agent instruction constraints and TASK+dependency-extract row validation and governance audits and human review.
Unknown values become TBD and are not guessed.
Agents must not invent scope items or dependency targets or parameter values or engineering content.
K-INVENT-1 is enforced by all agent instruction invariants and human review.
Conflicts between sources must be surfaced and not silently resolved.
Agents expose disagreements with pointers to the conflicting sources.
K-CONFLICT-1 is enforced by agent instruction invariants and human adjudication.
Claims and conclusions and characterizations must not overstate what the available warrant supports.
Statements of necessity and sufficiency and universality and completeness and exclusivity and direct regulatory conclusiveness require cited evidence that supports that strength.
Unsupported strong claims must be framed as interpretation or implementation-specific design or proposal.
K-CLAIM-1 is enforced by agent instruction constraints and governance audits and human review.
Every agent has an explicit write scope declared in its header block.
Agents do not write outside their declared zone.
K-WRITE-1 is enforced by the Agent Type table WRITE_SCOPE property and human review of diffs.
Task agent outputs to tool roots are immutable snapshots.
Pointer files named _LATEST.md may be overwritten.
Snapshot folders must not be overwritten.
K-SNAP-1 is enforced by agent instruction constraints and SPEC.md Section 11.
Agent instructions design-time checks constrain intent but do not guarantee behavior.
Agent instructions check K-GHOST-1 and K-WRITE-1 and K-SNAP-1 and K-PROV-1 and K-INVENT-1 and K-CONFLICT-1 and K-CLAIM-1 and K-DEP-1 and K-DEP-2.
ORCHESTRATOR runtime checks cover K-SEAL-1 and K-GATE-1 and K-HIER-1.
Human review gate checks cover K-AUTH-1 and K-AUTH-2 and K-BIND-1 and K-STALE-2 and K-MERGE-1 and K-VAL-1 and K-STATUS-1.
Future automated tooling checks cover K-STALE-1 and K-VAL-1 and K-MERGE-1 and K-AUTH-2 and K-DEP-2.
PROJECT_DECOMP decomposition checks cover K-HIER-1 and K-ID-1.
No invariants have been retired.
